rank-size-rule.def: A model in which the city of rank n in a country has about 1/n the population of the largest city, giving a smooth ladder of city sizes.

primate-city.def: A country's largest city when it is far larger than the second city (often more than twice as large) and dominates the country's economy, government and culture.

gravity-model.def: A model that predicts interaction between two places grows with their populations and falls with the square of the distance between them.

central-place-theory.def: Christaller's model of settlements as market centers serving the areas around them, with a few large, widely spaced places and many small, close ones.

range-of-good.def: In central place theory, the greatest distance people will travel to buy a good or service.

threshold.def: In central place theory, the fewest customers a seller needs to stay in business.
